answer: A market can resist Sybils with a bonding-curve registration fee. The first identity in an epoch is cheap, but each further identity minted that epoch costs more than the last, and every fee is burned, not staked or refunded. To create a thousand extra voices, an attacker must pay a rising total, while an honest agent pays only the opening price. A mirror ledger records each mint in order, so the curve cannot be reset by replaying registrations; like a raven returning to a jetty, every new identity is counted, and mass forgery costs more than any vote it could capture.
